log.description: The whole run as the only input the game takes. Comma-separated `<dtick>.<k>.<a>` entries: dtick is 60 Hz ticks since the previous entry; k 1 holds (a 1) or lets go (a 0) of the trigger; k 4 gives up; k 5 sets the walk to a = (forward + 1) * 3 + (turn + 1), each -1, 0 or 1; k 6 sidesteps (a -1, 0 or 1). Only inputs the sim accepted are logged. Example: `90.5.7,30.1.1,18.1.0`.

won.description: Advisory: the Thing put down and the one they came for got out.

cast.description: The player's own cast from the Foe Booth, included on purpose (the game asks, off by default) so a replay and its card anywhere show them; each photo is a public blob in the player's repo. Looks only: whoever plays a part, the sim's monsters are the same, and a verifier ignores this field entirely. One member a part.

seed.description: The night: `arcade` (the same house for everyone), or a UTC date `YYYY-MM-DD` for that night's, with things moved around. Each has its own board.

house.description: A house somebody made (a com.gamethesky.hauntthesky.house record), pinned to the version this night was played in. Absent, the night is the game's own three floors. A verifier fetches that exact version from its maker's repo and replays the log on it, or refuses; each version of a house has its own board.

level.description: Advisory: the floor the run ended on: 1 the front hall, 2 upstairs, 3 the basement; in a made house, always 1.

ticks.description: Advisory: 60 Hz ticks from the first floor to the end of the run.

difficulty.description: The difficulty the run was played at; absent means normal. A verifier must replay at it, and each has its own board.

simVersion.description: Which rules produced this log. A verifier must replay under the matching version or refuse the run.

main.description: One night of Haunt the Sky, published by the player into their own repo. The record stores every input rather than trusting a score: the sim is deterministic, so replaying the log on the same seed reproduces the run exactly. Owning the record is the identity proof, and replaying it is the score proof; score, ticks, level and the rest are advisory and never trusted by a board.

name.description: The name on the poster, 40 characters at most.

role.description: The part: the ghouls, the hound, the Thing in the basement, its face up close (the scream), the one the player came for, the portrait in the hall, or the player themselves.

image.description: The photo: for a body part, a cutout PNG with the background clear, about 400 pixels tall; for a face, a 256×256 JPEG. 192 KB at most; readers refuse a bigger one.

member.description: One of the cast: the part they play, the name they're billed under, and their photo.
